title: Why Do Traffic Jams Appear Out of Nowhere?
description:
No crash, no roadworks, no lane closed, and still you stop. Physicists rebuilt the mystery on a 230 m ring road with 22 cars and the jam appeared anyway.
Here is the wave that causes it, why it runs backwards, and how one calm car can dissolve it.

Chapters
0:00 A jam with no cause
0:44 The ring-road experiment
1:30 A jam is a wave
2:30 The chain of late reactions
3:41 Why only when it's crowded
4:41 One calm car
5:56 The answer

Sources
- Sugiyama et al. (2008), Traffic jams without bottlenecks, New Journal of Physics 10, 033001
- Stern et al. (2018), Dissipation of stop-and-go waves via control of autonomous vehicles, Transportation Research Part C 89 — https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.01693
- Bando et al. (1995), Dynamical model of traffic congestion, Physical Review E 51, 1035
- Green (2000), How long does it take to stop?, Transportation Human Factors 2(3)
- Helbing (2001), Traffic and related self-driven many-particle systems, Reviews of Modern Physics 73

Have you ever been stuck in a jam with no cause? Tell me where in the comments.

Script, voice and animation are AI-produced (Claude; Kokoro voice). Every number is checked against the sources above.
